description: Add Battle AI feature - database schema, backend API routes, and frontend page. This is a new BETA feature that allows users to configure an AI avatar (via HeyGen Streaming Avatar API) to join their TikTok live. Includes session management table, admin configuration for available avatars/pricing/plan restrictions, and user-facing page with avatar configuration and 'Join Live' button.
steps: 1. Create lib/db/src/schema/battle-ai.ts with battle_ai_sessions table (id, userId, status [idle/streaming/error], avatarConfig JSON [appearance, voice, gender, personality], tiktokUsername, rtmpUrl, heygenSessionId, startedAt, endedAt, createdAt, updatedAt) and battle_ai_config table (id, availableAvatars JSON array, pricePerSession, planRestrictions JSON, maxSessionDuration, enabled boolean, updatedAt). Export types.

3. Create artifacts/api-server/src/lib/battle-ai-store.ts with CRUD functions: getBattleAiConfig, upsertBattleAiConfig, createSession, getSessionsByUser, getSessionById, updateSession, getAllSessions (admin). Use in-memory store pattern like other stores in the project.

4. Create artifacts/api-server/src/routes/battle-ai.ts with routes: GET /battle-ai/config (public config for users), POST /battle-ai/sessions (create session - requireAuth), GET /battle-ai/sessions (user's sessions - requireAuth), POST /battle-ai/sessions/:id/start (activate avatar streaming - requireAuth), POST /battle-ai/sessions/:id/stop (stop streaming - requireAuth), GET /battle-ai/admin/config (admin get full config - requireAdmin), PUT /battle-ai/admin/config (admin update config - requireAdmin), GET /battle-ai/admin/sessions (admin list all sessions - requireAdmin). The /start endpoint should mock the HeyGen API call (placeholder with HEYGEN_API_KEY env check) and return a streaming status.

6. Create artifacts/creatools/src/pages/battle-ai.tsx - a full page with: hero section showing BETA badge, avatar configuration panel (select appearance/voice/gender from available options loaded from API), personality text input, TikTok username input (pre-filled from user context), RTMP URL input, 'Entrar na Live' button that calls the start endpoint, session history list, status indicators (idle/streaming/error). Use the project's glassmorphism design (glass-card, neon-glow-cyan, stat-card classes). Include animated elements.
7. Add Battle AI route to artifacts/creatools/src/App.tsx - import the page and add route /battle-ai with ProtectedRoute wrapper

8. Add Battle AI nav item to the DEFAULT_SECTIONS in artifacts/creatools/src/components/layout/app-layout.tsx - add to 'ferramentas' section with icon 'Sparkles', badge 'BETA' with color '#ef4444', href '/battle-ai'
acceptance_criteria: lib/db/src/schema/battle-ai.ts exports battle_ai_sessions and battle_ai_config table definitions
Backend routes for battle-ai are registered and handle all specified endpoints
Frontend page renders with avatar configuration, session controls, and BETA badge
Navigation sidebar includes Battle AI link with BETA badge
pnpm run build succeeds without type errors
verification: Run pnpm run typecheck from workspace root and confirm no errors
Run pnpm run build from workspace root and confirm successful build
findings: Pre-existing typecheck errors in admin.tsx (AnalyticsSection, WebhooksSection, RateLimitsSection, DevToolsSection not found) - not introduced by this feature. Build requires PORT and BASE_PATH env vars (PORT=3000 BASE_PATH=/). Node setup required libatomic1 and mise trust. The routes/index.ts already had uncommitted changes adding analytics, webhooks-admin, dev-tools, and rate-limits routers.
